items.content: Below, the cities are scattered like shattered glass across black velvet, each cluster of light a human story compressed into a glowing smear. The wing cuts through thin, cold air, trembling almost imperceptibly, and beyond the scratched oval of the window the darkness feels absolute and ancient. You press your forehead against the plastic and watch a lone highway unspool like a lit thread through nothing, carrying its small bright cargo of headlights somewhere urgent, somewhere that cannot possibly matter from this height.

items.content: The theatre holds its breath around her, vast and velvet-dark, smelling of something sweetly stale and decades old. She is the only one here, a single warm body in a cavern built for crowds, and the emptiness feels less like loneliness than like privilege. The screen glows a soft, patient grey. She wraps her coat tighter, tucks her feet beneath her, and waits for the world she came to borrow.

items.content: The last miles dissolved beneath weary feet like sugar in warm water, and something loosened in the chest — a knot tied so long ago its origins had been forgotten. Home appeared not with fanfare but with the quiet certainty of a word finally remembered, hovering at the edge of recognition before settling into place. He stood at the threshold and understood, perhaps for the first time, that arrival is not a moment but a slow exhale — the body releasing what the mind had carried alone for so very long.
